claim: There is a mechanism for forcing a monochromatic triangle under a colouring of the edges of a clique-free graph by infinitely many colours, other than induction on the number of colours, diagonalization over colourings, or a partition-calculus pigeonhole producing a large monochromatic clique.
domain: partition calculus / infinite Ramsey theory / clique-free arrowing

facets.entities: K4-free and clique-free graphs at uncountable cardinals, edge colourings by infinitely many colours, monochromatic triangles
facets.mechanism: arrowing of a clique-free host for infinitely many colours; forcing a monochromatic triangle without producing a large monochromatic clique
facets.method: partition relations for graphs, Nesetril-Rodl amalgamation at infinite cardinals, elementary submodel arguments, forcing and iterated forcing for Ramsey properties, stepping-up lemmas
facets.outcome: an infinite-colour arrowing theorem for a clique-free host, or a proof that none exists
